entry_state: Review decisions preserve source history, and identity distinguishes evidence, model and run changes. Adapter examples show why successful conversion can lose context, omit pages or duplicate numeric transformations. Source-byte identity, visible readings, structural checks and execution validation remain separate; the inline-value subsection continues on the next page.
exit_state: Chapter 13 closes by preserving raw occurrences, typed values, contextual comparison and optional reduced views. The Apple example connects actual source identities without inferring general validation or historical availability. Native Arelle and a deterministic PDF comparator are selected as source-grounded first paths; environment resolution, executed compatibility and distribution conditions remain separate. Acceptance criteria and sequencing follow next.
findings: Equal displayed amounts, typed equality, duplicate membership and interval consistency are different operations.
The Apple comparative examples preserve multiple locations and correct sign and scale without double counting equity.
Source selection, resolved environment and executed compatibility are explicitly different evidence levels. No new confirmed manuscript defect.
